calls.head: Special teams lean toward the Oilers
calls.body: The Maple Leafs’ penalty kill is near the bottom of the league, and the Oilers’ power play is one of the best. Discipline matters more than usual for the Maple Leafs tonight. Edmonton has had one of the league’s most effective power plays for years.
calls.call: The Oilers’ power play creates at least their usual 9.4 expected goals per 60.

EDM.head: We leaned Edmonton’s way (57%), and they came through.

surprises.head: Edmonton couldn’t get good looks
surprises.body: Edmonton usually gets worse looks than most teams. Even by those standards, this was a night of harmless shots: a 3.6% chance of scoring on the average shot at 5-on-5, against their usual 6.0% and a league average of 6.3%. A team strays this far about once every 40 games.

surprises.head: Devon Levi stole one with a shutout
surprises.body: Levi stopped all 19 shots, worth 1.2 expected goals. That is more than Edmonton’s winning margin. Starting goalies have a night this good about once every 5 starts.

story.head: Levi slams the door on the Maple Leafs
paras: Brandon Duhaime and Colton Dach squared off midway through the first. Evan Bouchard scored the only goal of the game late in the second.

Nothing much separated these two on the chances. This one could have gone either way. Devon Levi made 19 saves for his first NHL shutout. Anthony Stolarz stopped 22 of 23 for the Maple Leafs. Levi has won five straight starts. The Oilers improved to 15-3-3, still first in the Pacific, while the Leafs dropped to 8-12-2, sinking to the bottom of the Atlantic.
